facts.text: Mel's Skate Shop has traded since 2012.
Mel's own site states: We were the first roller derby shop to open in South Africa.
Mel's fits skates in person and runs a custom/special-order path for sizes not held in stock.
Roll-Line's own dealer database lists Mel's Skate Shop, and Mel's is its only South African dealer.
Roadhouse Roller Rink names Mel's its "RECOMMENDED SHOP".
Roadhouse Roller Rink is at Eastgate Shopping Centre, Bedfordview.
Roadhouse Roller Rink publishes R100 entry, R150 with rental skates, R190 with skates plus full pads.
Mel's has one public review anywhere: Elizabeth de Lange, Facebook, 2 November 2022.
Four South African roller derby leagues are confirmed: Golden City Rollers (Johannesburg, 2010), Durban Roller Derby (2012), Cape Town Rollergirls and P-Town Roller Derby.
Roller Skates: 98 products.
Roller Derby: 8 products.
Artistic Roller Skates: 48 products.
Recreational Roller Skates: 71 products.
Adjustable Roller Skates: 17 products.
Available in smaller/kids sizes: 30 products.
Ice Skates: 35 products.
Ice Blades: 2 products.
Ice Accessories: 10 products.
Inline Skates: 28 products.
Protective Gear / Sets: 27 products.
Wheels and Bearings: 38 products.
Toe Stops/Jam plugs: 17 products.
Aura Sky 100 Ice Skate Boot White is R12,050.
Aura Sky 50 Ice Skate Boot White is R7,850.
Aura Sky 200 Ice Skate Boot White is R15,550.

The demo shows the white Sky 100, product id 11919. The black record, id 11938, is a WooCommerce duplicate: its slug ends -white-copy and its only boot photo is the Sky 200's, so it is not used or linked.
Aura Sky boots are imported specifically on order and are not kept in stock, with an approx. 2-week lead time.

Approx. 2 weeks beats almost every made-to-order boot benchmarked: Bont 6-8 weeks semi-custom and 8-12 full custom, Riedell ice full custom 12-14 weeks, Riedell ColorLab 8-10 weeks plus shipping, Jackson 6-8 weeks modified.
Mel's product page states the price is as of 30 July 2026 and may move with the exchange rate.
Mel's product page says the heat-mould is fitted only by phoning the shop directly.

Aura publishes the heat-mould as a requirement, not an option: AURA skates must always be heat molded. The carbon construction lets the boot expand in width and volume and conform to the foot, and the boots are designed to fit very snug before moulding.
AURA skates are sized in millimeters from 210-300 mm and are designed to be heat molded for a custom fit.

Aura's full per-model size run is published on Mel's own size-chart page, with a per-size width grid for each of Sky 50, Sky 100 and Sky 200 in men's and women's fits. The grids print four width columns B, C, D and E, but offer E in no size at all; men's fits are C and D only, women's fits add B.
Which Sky to order comes from Aura's own selection matrix: foot-length band in millimetres crossed with body weight and jump level, giving Sky 50, Sky 100 or Sky 200.
Aura sizes from the Brannock Suggested Size, not raw foot length alone. The suggested size is a High-Performance fit; add 1/2 size, 5 mm, for a Comfort fit.
Aura's key rule: if the skate feels tight, move up in width before increasing length.
Aura publishes an optimal blade size in inches for every boot size from 210 mm to 300 mm.

Spec table: boot only, blade sold separately; carbon construction; heat-mouldable and required to be; sized in millimetres from 210 to 300; widths C and D in men's fits and B, C and D in women's fits, the E column being printed on Aura's grids but offered in no size. Level and stiffness are published nowhere reachable and are left out rather than guessed. Which of these sizes and widths Mel can actually order is hers to confirm.
Mel's size-chart page carries no HTML table at all: every brand chart on it is published as an image.
Roll-Line, one of Mel's two flagship lines, has no size table on the size-chart page.

Riedell and Sure-Grip each have a tab on Mel's size-chart page, but neither publishes a size table. Riedell's tab sends the buyer off-site to Riedell's own sizing pages, and its roller link is broken as published, truncated to "/Support/Sizing-Hel". Sure-Grip's tab carries Mel's own measuring method and a printable insole chart PDF on her domain - her most personal sizing content, but not something a size finder can read. Both are brands a derby or recreational buyer would be offered.
Brands differ by 1-2 full sizes for the same foot, so a finder result is a starting point, not a fitting.
Rio Roller: UK 11J to 12, EU 29 to 47, insole length 200 mm to 300 mm.
SFR Galaxy: UK J10 to 10A, EU 28 to 44.5, foot length 166 mm to 302 mm, with a ball-girth column.
Chaya Emerald: US 4 to 13, UK 3.5 to 12, 227 mm to 289 mm.
Chaya Sapphire: US 4 to 15, UK 2 to 13, 228 mm to 301 mm.
Atom Vertigo boot chart, all models (Q6, Q4, F1): US women's 4 to 12 with a wider unisex run 6 to 13, 217 mm to 294 mm, EU 36.5 to 46.5.
The Pilot F-16 derby plate chart maps plate size 5.0 to 8.5, axle to axle, onto Q-4/Q-6, F-1 and Jackson boot sizes, with plate length 218 mm to 309 mm.

Powerslide, Playlife, Jackson, Destiny and S1 each publish a chart on Mel's size-chart page as an image, as does a second SFR model in a tab titled "SFR Vision" - so SFR has two model charts and only the Galaxy one is transcribed. Those images are not transcribed here and the finder hands off to WhatsApp for them.
Interactive size calculators are rare: across 26 shop teardowns only ProSkaters Place and Pigeon's ship one.
Mel's publishes by-appointment hours: Wed 12:00-18:00 through Sun 09:30-16:00.
Mel's phone is +27 82 370 6771, the same number on WhatsApp.
Mel's email is melony@melsskateshop.co.za.
Mel's Facebook page is facebook.com/melsskateshopofficial.
R100 Gauteng · R150 elsewhere · 1-3 days.

Mel's own pages disagree on shipping: the homepage says R100 Gauteng and R150 elsewhere, /shipping-information/ says R100 JHB/PTA and R180 other regions. This demo uses the homepage figures everywhere.
Mel's Book An Appointment link leaves the site for Koalendar, and /book-an-appointment/ returns 404.
On-domain booking with named service types is rare: of 16 new teardowns, 4 route booking off-domain and 5 have no booking at all.
/contact-us/ and /book-an-appointment/ both 404; the working contact page is /contact/, and it carries no address, no map and no social links.
Mel's ships a hidden "No results" live-search placeholder on /shop/ and on two category pages.
Every social icon on Mel's current site links to # rather than to a real profile.
One Mel's product line carries an ad-hoc back-in-stock note. There is no systematic notify-me.
Mel's interleaves sold-out accessories with in-stock R12,050 boots and offers no waitlist.
PayJustNow is Pay-in-3 at 0%.
Whether Mel's can offer PayJustNow is unsettled: confirming PayJustNow and Ozow SME onboarding terms is an open question in the report.
Mel's offers no instalments today, against a catalogue topping out at R15,550.

Mel's Fit Guarantee — if it doesn't fit, we exchange it. 30 days, unworn outdoors. What qualifies: unworn outdoors, original box, guards unfitted. Who pays the courier each way is stated. To start it, one WhatsApp message with the order number. No fit-based exchange on custom or imported-to-order boots — size confirmed with us on WhatsApp before we order.
or 3 interest-free instalments of R4,016.67 — PayJustNow, once onboarded.
Fitting prices: Quad fitting R350 · Ice boot fitting + heat-mould R850 · Kids fitting R250 · Video consult R200.
Fitting durations: Quad fitting 30 min · Ice boot fitting + heat-mould 60 min · Kids fitting 20 min · Video consult 20 min.
Move or cancel a fitting up to 24 hours before, by WhatsApp, at no charge; after that the fitting fee is due.
Heat-mould & fit in store — R850. Mel says on her own product page that these boots must be heat moulded and that she fits it, so the service is real; the price is ours.
Mail-in heat-mould — R650 + courier. A pre-ship bake rather than a foot-in-boot mould. Whether Mel does a mail-in bake at all is a question for the call.

Per-size stock states on the Aura size selector — in stock, imported to order with a lead time, or notify me. The size run and its widths are real and published by Aura; which size is on a shelf on any given day is not published anywhere, so the states are structure, not stock truth.
The buy button is a demo. Cart and checkout land in month 1; order this boot on WhatsApp now.

Home hero positioning line and its Roll-Line note, in Melony's voice. Four clauses, each already a sourced fact: trading since 2012, first roller derby shop in South Africa, official Roll-Line dealer, fitted in person. Place is given as Gauteng only - decision #504 struck the suburb because neither published address survived scrutiny. Lives in draft-copy.json at home.hero.

Promise-row labels and notes on Home: the courier label, the Fit Guarantee label and its one-line terms note, the Roll-Line dealer label and the WhatsApp label. The wording is ours; every figure is pointed at contact.json or at the fit-guarantee entry rather than retyped. Lives at home.promiseRow.

Home Size Finder CTA band plus the six discipline-card blurbs and the in-stock section heading and note. One sentence each, saying what the shop fits rather than describing categories. Counts stay with store:categories; these are the words around them. Lives at home.sizeFinderBand, home.disciplines and home.inStock.

Home trust-row card labels and notes: the Roll-Line dealer card, the Roadhouse Roller Rink recommended-shop card carrying "Eastgate, Bedfordview" as the rink's own location, and the one-review card attributed to Elizabeth de Lange, Facebook, 2 Nov 2022. The review copy says plainly that it is the only public review and refuses to imply others. Lives at home.trustRow.

Derby hub category description, 105 words, in Melony's voice: who the hub is for, what the shop holds for derby using the real store:categories counts, what the decision actually is, and the order to work it in. Lives at derby.categoryCopy.

The four derby FAQ answers. What size (measure, plus the 1-2 size variance and the honest no-table position on Riedell and Sure-Grip); which plate size (wheelbase axle to axle, the published Pilot F-16 chart, and no Roll-Line plate table anywhere); wheel hardness for Roadhouse versus tarmac (the soft-grips / hard-slides principle, an explicit refusal to print a durometer number, and a handoff to Melony - the report names Roadhouse's surface as an open unknown); and what a league kit list needs (the six standard items, the four leagues named as leagues that exist, per-league lists coming in the build). Lives at derby.faq.

Derby hub control copy: the five decision-card labels, the in-stock toggle label and note, the result-count template and its empty first-render state, the empty-state line, the stock-state labels, the sold-out "Tell us your deadline" handoff, and the league line plus the Roadhouse credential attribution. Lives at derby.filters, derby.stock, derby.credential and derby.links.

PDP top banner and gallery captions: imported to order at approx. 2 weeks, the price-as-of date and exchange-rate caveat, size confirmed on WhatsApp before ordering and no fit-based exchange on an imported boot; plus the black-record colour note and the four gallery captions including the labelled empty fit-video slot. Lives at pdp.banner, pdp.colourNote and pdp.gallery.

The PDP fit note - Melony on how this boot actually fits. Carbon, built snug before moulding, the mould as a requirement rather than an upgrade, sizing from the Brannock suggested size with the half-size comfort allowance, and width before length. Every clause traces to an aura-* entry. Lives at pdp.fitNote, with the same rules echoed shorter at pdp.sizes.brannockNote.

The three PDP question-and-answer pairs: what a heat-mould is, can I cancel, and what if it doesn't fit. The third quotes the drafted guarantee terms by reference to shared.fitGuarantee rather than retyping them, so there is one canonical copy of the terms in the demo. Lives at pdp.qa.

PDP commerce copy: the honest buy-button label, the demo sheet (cart and checkout land in month 1, order on WhatsApp now) and its two actions, the fulfilment line pointing at the courier fixture, the two service-checkbox labels and their notes, the spec-table note, the instalment note, the rail titles and the two calls to action including "Ask Melony about this boot". Lives at pdp.buyButtonLabel, pdp.demoSheet, pdp.fulfilment, pdp.services, pdp.specTableNote and the pdp cta keys.

Size Finder instruction copy: the three step headings, the picker labels, the five-step heel-to-wall method written to be followed on a phone with a pencil, the alternative inputs, the "Which Sky?" instruction, and the result lead with the 1-2 size variance disclaimer pointed at sizes.json. Lives at finder.steps, finder.measure, finder.whichSky and finder.result.

Size Finder dead-end copy: the out-of-range fallback pointed at sizes.json plus the note that the WhatsApp message already carries the measurement, and the no-table handoff written honestly per decision #507 - Roll-Line has no table anywhere, Riedell's tab sends the buyer off-site with one broken link, and Sure-Grip's tab is a printable insole chart a calculator cannot read. Names no brand that does not exist. Lives at finder.handoffs.

Book a fitting copy: the page lede, the pre-appointment intake block written to agree with every bring array in fittings.json, the three-step promise and the cancellation policy both pointed at fittings.json rather than re-worded, the by-appointment availability line built on Mel's own published hours with no walk-in claim anywhere, and the form labels ending in "Request via WhatsApp" with the honest on-domain-calendar note. Lives at booking.*.

The full drafted Fit Guarantee prose: the named one-liner, the promise-row short terms, the three literal lines (what qualifies, who pays the courier each way, how to start it) and the imported-and-custom carve-out. This is the prose of the same promise the fit-guarantee entry compresses; the chip stays on that entry and this copy carries none. Lives at shared.fitGuarantee.

The chip legend sentence - the caption that explains what the proposed stamp means, shown visibly above the first chip on every page that has one and referenced by aria-describedby from every chipped element. It says plainly that the marked item is something Mel has not published and that we drafted it. Lives at shared.chipLegend.

Shared chrome strings: the header brand and five nav labels plus the skip link, the contact-block field labels with the Gauteng-only place note and the WhatsApp-is-fastest note, the WhatsApp labels including the floating button, the demo note and the image credit. Lives at shared.header, shared.contact, shared.whatsapp, shared.demoNote and shared.imageCredit.
